questions: Q1: Is the CLI implementation code already in place on the branch?
Q2: What quality gates must pass for the helix-cli changes?
Q3: How should the CLI commands be verified without a running server?

answers.answer: Yes, all CLI implementation code is confirmed in place by diagnosis. Two new files (inspect/netsuite.ts at 60 lines, run/index.ts at 53 lines) and two modified router files (inspect/index.ts case 'netsuite' at lines 125-138, index.ts case 'run' at lines 101-105) are all implemented following existing hxFetch patterns.

answers.answer: Two quality gates: (1) typecheck via `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), (2) build via `npm run build` (tsc). Tests via `npm test` (tsc && node --test dist/**/*.test.js) should also pass, though no existing inspect handler tests exist as precedent. Zero runtime npm dependencies.

answers.answer: The CLI can be type-checked and built independently of the server. Static verification: confirm exports (cmdNetsuite, cmdRun), router wiring (case statements), and help text inclusion. After building, run `node dist/index.js --help` and `node dist/index.js inspect --help` to verify new commands appear. End-to-end testing against the server is a cross-repo concern covered by the server plan's CHK-08.
